items.title: The Suns have a few scores to settle this season
items.content:
Phoenix Suns' Devin Booker front drives past Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Doncic during the 2024-2025 NBA regular season match between Los Angeles Lakers and Phoenix Suns in Los Angeles, the United States, March 16, 2025. (Photo by Ringo Chiu/Xinhua via Getty Images)	We are a week away from the NBA schedule release, according to recent reporting from NBA insider Marc Stein. Which means it’s time to look ahead to the most anticipated Phoenix Suns matchups. Sure, we don’t know the schedule, but we know who the opponents are, so let’s take a crack at projecting the spiciest matchups based on last season’s games and Phoenix’s history against other franchises.

Building off some exciting games in the Luka Doncic Lakers eraPlaying five times last year, the Phoenix Suns faced only the Thunder more often than the Lakers last season (if you include the postseason, 9 times against OKC last season). In five matchups, the Suns took the season series 3-2, with two of the five games coming down to the final possession.

With LeBron James on the Sixers, Devin Booker and Luka Doncic become the matchup’s headliners, just as they were when Doncic was on the Mavericks and the two built a rivalry after Dallas beat the Suns in a dramatic second-round series in 2022.

Divisional rivals, the franchises have met 13 times in the postseason, with the most recent matchup coming in 2021, when Phoenix won in six games. After a second straight 50-win season, Los Angeles revamped its roster around Dončić and Austin Reaves, signing Walker Kessler, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton.

Against Booker, Doncic consistently brings his best, averaging three points per game more than his career average. Booker also scores more than his career average when he plays against Luka.

Can the Suns have more success against the champs?The Suns swept their season series against the Knicks last season. While Finals MVP Jalen Brunson didn’t play in the second matchup, when he suited up for the first contest, strong play from Devin Booker late and a 20-point first half from Dillon Brooks catapulted the team to victory over the eventual NBA champions.

Phoenix went 7-11 against the top three seeds in the Eastern and Western Conferences during the regular season and was swept by the West’s top-seeded Thunder in the first round of the playoffs. The Knicks were the only one of those six teams against which the Suns had a winning record.

Despite big man Mitchell Robinson leaving to join the Celtics, New York’s roster remains mostly unchanged, with the team retaining key free agents Landry Shamet and Jordan Clarkson. The team’s performance against the defending champions could potentially be used as an indicator of its ceiling during the 2026-27 campaign.

items.title: Stacey King's cause of death revealed as tributes to Bulls icon continue
items.content:
The cause of death of Stacey King, the late Chicago Bulls star who died in June, has been revealed.

A Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office spokesperson confirmed on Friday, Aug. 7 to USA TODAY Sports that King died June 7 of hypertensive cardiovascular disease, which is a complication of long-term high blood pressure. Obesity was also cited as a contributing factor.

King died in his home in River Forest, Illinois. He was 59.

After his death, tributes poured in from all corners of the basketball world.

In the Chicago neighborhood of Logan Square, which is northwest of downtown, a mural was painted to honor him.

The mural depicts a close-up of King’s face against a black background. To his right, a silhouette of the Bulls logo wears a crown, in homage to King’s last name.

One of King’s broadcast catchphrases – “Too big, too strong, too fast, too good” – is captioned to the left of the mural.

Stacey King: forever a Chicago legend👑

📍 2929 West Fullerton

Mural by @BigWallSignspic.twitter.com/CTAdVNLPrK

— Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) August 3, 2026King played eight seasons in the NBA from 1989-97, five of which came with the Bulls. The sixth pick out of Oklahoma in the 1989 draft, King was a 6-foot-11 big man who won three NBA championships alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen in his first five seasons in Chicago.

He later played stints with the Minnesota Timberwolves, Miami Heat, Dallas Mavericks and Boston Celtics.

King averaged 6.4 points, 3.3 rebounds and 0.9 assists across his 438 career games.

After his playing career ended, he joined the team’s broadcast crew in 2006 and became its color commentator. He was the voice that a generation of Bulls fans grew up hearing, even the reason some tuned in at all during a lot of lean years.

"Stacey King was a cherished member of the Bulls family and one of the truly unique personalities in our organization's history," Bulls chairman Jerry Reinsdorf said June 7 in a statement. "His connection to Chicago, the Bulls and our fans spanned more than three decades – first as a player and later as the unmistakable voice that helped bring Bulls basketball into the homes of generations of fans."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Stacey King's cause of death revealed as tributes to Bulls icon continue

items.title: Wizards To Sign Alondes Williams
items.content:
The Wizards and free agent guard Alondes Williams have agreed to terms on a deal, agent Daniel Hazan tells NBA insider Chris Haynes (Twitter link).

Haynes doesn’t provide any specifics on the terms of the agreement, but given that Williams has no two-way eligibility left and has never been on a standard NBA contract, it seems safe to assume it’ll be a non-guaranteed training camp deal that includes Exhibit 9 and Exhibit 10 language.

Williams, who went undrafted out of Wake Forest in 2022, has bounced back and forth between the NBA and G League over the past four years, spending time with the Nets, Heat, Pistons, and Wizards, as well as their respective NBAGL affiliates.

The 6’4″ guard has only made 13 appearances at the NBA level, but he earned rotation minutes while on a 10-day deal with Washington in February of this year, averaging 11.0 points per game on .615/.357/.875 shooting in four appearances off the bench. That stretch included a 25-point, 10-rebound performance in a win over Indiana on Feb. 20.

A stalwart at the G League level over the last few seasons, Williams set a new career high by scoring 22.5 points per game in 35 outings for the Capital City Go-Go in 2025/26. The 26-year-old also contributed 5.5 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1.5 steals per game. In 2023/24, he was named the G League’s Most Improved Player and claimed a spot on the All-NBAGL first team.

There could be a path for Williams to earn a spot on the Wizards’ opening night roster this fall, given that the team is currently carrying 14 players on standard contracts. But unless he has a huge preseason, it seems more likely that he’ll return to the Go-Go to open the season.
